text:
Trump spoke about American exceptionalism during his time at Mt. Rushmore(Image: Getty Images)

After multiple wins for progressive candidates in recent primaries, President Donald Trump criticized communism during a speech at Mount Rushmore on Friday evening.

"There is now a resurgence of the communist menace in our land, including from newcomers to our country, who embrace ideas totally opposed to our way of life and our great success," he said under the carved faces of former presidents.

Trump called communism "a mortal threat to American liberty" worse than September 11, "the enemy of the Constitution," "the enemy of July 4, 1776," and "the enemy" overall.

"So, on the eve of this 250th anniversary of American heritage, we resolve and swear for all to hear that the citizens of the United States of America will vanquish communism quickly," Trump said, adding, "Don’t let them take too much of your time."

Trump has addressed the longstanding rumors that he wants to be on the monument(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Trump's comments come after recent a clean sweep for Mamdani-backed candidates in New York's Democratic primary. Brad Lander defeated U.S. congressman Dan Goldman in his primary election, Assemblywoman Claire Valdez defeated Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso in the 7th district of New York, and Darializa Avila Chevalier, a doctoral student who has joined pro-Palestinian protests at Columbia University, won her race in the state's 13th district. All were backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Trump appeared to reference Mamdani's endorsements in a late-night post on social media following the elections, saying America would "never be a communist country!"

“There would be no better addition to the iconic Mount Rushmore than the 45th and 47th President of the United States, Donald Trump,” Taylor Rogers, a White House spokeswoman, said in a statement to The Washington Post ahead of tonight’s event.

Soon after he first took office in 2017, Trump told a congresswoman in private that it was his dream to see his face on the monument. That congresswoman turned out to be Kristi Noem, who would become South Dakota's governor and gift Trump a sculpture depicting his face on Mount Rushmore next to Lincoln’s. He put the statuette on display at his Mar-a-Lago office.

Trump last visited the monument six years ago, delivering a speech on July 3, 2020, that he hoped would rally his supporters around the law-and-order message he centered his second campaign around — and failed to give him the White House again in 2021.

“Never suggested it,” he wrote on Twitter in 2020, responding to a New York Times report that said a White House aide had inquired with Noem’s office about the process of carving additional presidents. But Trump continued: “Although, based on all of the many things accomplished during the first 3 1/2 years, perhaps more than any other Presidency, sounds like a good idea to me!”

There was hail and thunder ahead of Trump's remarks(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A year before that, when he was asked by The Hill if he’d like to see his face carved on Mount Rushmore, Trump replied that he didn’t want to say: “If I answer that question, ‘Yes,’ I will end up with such bad publicity.”

At a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, in 2017, Trump stated that each of the presidents on Mount Rushmore “believed in protecting American industry.” Again, the idea of his joining them was presented, and he insisted he wouldn’t mention it — though he did.

“If I did it joking, totally joking, having fun, the fake news media will say, ‘He believes he should be on Mount Rushmore,’” Trump said. “So I won’t say it, okay? I won’t say it.”

Days after he was sworn in for a second time in January 2025, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-Florida) filed a bill directing the Interior Department to start the process of having Trump’s face carved onto Mount Rushmore. Then, last July, Rep. Andy Ogles (R-Tennessee) sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum asking him to “explore” adding Trump, noting that “past bureaucratic resistance or political discomfort” should not stop the process.
